prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its translation into long-acting incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I have changed my third name from Mojsov to Knudsen, and I want the reason on record. Round 1 showed that the question is not who matters more but what the citation says the discovery was. GLP-1 is not only a hormone story. Holst's human physiology and Drucker's proglucagon and intestinotropic biology established the mechanism, and Knudsen's acylation and albumin-binding design solved the half-life problem that kept a peptide with a half-life of minutes from becoming liraglutide and semaglutide. The clinical evidence the prize would rest on, from large independent outcome trials in type 2 diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal disease, comes from those analogues. A citation honouring both physiology and translation describes the whole arc, and each of the three names has a distinct, non-overlapping and decisive contribution. The mechanism is stable and replicated, and I see no maturity objection to the core claim.
statement.case_against: Four credible names go into three places, and whichever is dropped, the allocation is contestable. With Knudsen, Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active truncated peptide goes unrecognised, and Habener sits outside the supplied credit list. I cannot settle the priority record from the evidence provided, and I do not claim the question is closed. The other reservation is whether an industrial drug-design contribution belongs next to two academic discoverers in a Physiology or Medicine citation. I now think it does, because the physiology alone did not change practice. Long-term safety of the incretin class is still accumulating, and I cannot verify the newest outcome data from the file. I do not see that as an obstacle to the prize.

responses.point: The chair says he moved from Drucker, Holst and Mojsov to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, but would accept Mojsov if the committee prefers a discovery-only citation and the reasoning is stated. He also argues that a contested edge is not a contested core.
responses.response: I agree with the last point. Holst and Drucker are secure under every reading, so the uncertainty about the third name should not delay or weaken the prize. I have followed you to Knudsen. In round 1 I argued for the discovery trio as the cleaner citation. On reflection, the cleanliness comes at a cost, because the priority record on the active peptide is the least settled part of the story, and I proposed settling it from documents I do not have. A citation built on the better documented contributions is the more defensible one. I would not block a Mojsov version if the committee wants discovery only, but the committee should record why, as you say.

responses.point: Perlmann answered my round-1 position by saying that priority disputes are a reason to anchor the citation in physiology and therapeutic development, and that drug design is not a lesser category, because half-life extension and albumin binding were real conceptual work and past prizes have recognised translation.
responses.response: This moved me. I had treated Knudsen's work as drug development resting on an established discovery, which understated it. Acylation to engage albumin binding is a design principle, not routine optimisation, and it is what turned the hormone into a therapy with outcome data. Your point that the credit lines are clearer on that side than on the early peptide work is also fair, and it undercuts my earlier case for Mojsov. I still think the Mojsov claim is real. That is a limitation of the three-person cap, not a reason to pretend the claim is weak.

responses.point: Linnarsson argues that a prize stopping at hormone biology omits the step that made the discovery matter to patients, because Drucker and Holst already cover discovery and physiology, so replacing Knudsen with Mojsov would leave the translation unrecognised. He also says B031 is weaker than B014 or B006 this year because STING-targeted drugs have not shown clear clinical benefit.
responses.response: On GLP-1 you persuaded me, and your point that the two academics already cover discovery and physiology is the one that decided it. On B031 I accept the maturity concern. I held it as an alternative and not a preferred prize for the same reason. Interferon-driven disease is where cGAS-STING may matter clinically, and the mechanism is firm, but I cannot point to clear patient benefit from STING modulation yet. I still think Chen and Barber is the right credit if it comes forward, and I share your worry about earlier cyclic dinucleotide work complicating the priority statement.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks optogenetics second, proposes Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel, and in the chair's questions the committee is asked whether a single-topic B014 prize is preferable to pairing it with a second achievement such as B006 or B008.
responses.response: I would keep B014 as a single part. A pairing would not strengthen it, and the three-person cap would force a cut in one of the two parts. Optogenetics is where I am least persuaded as a second part. The science is exceptional, but six names have credible claims, and a Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel trio leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck. I also see it mainly as an enabling method, so the case for a medical prize depends on how the committee weighs methods against therapies. If we did pair, I would look first at B006, where durable remissions are documented, before B008.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will record the third GLP-1 name as Knudsen on the grounds of translation, or choose Mojsov on discovery grounds, and whether the reasoning will be stated explicitly.
How Mojsov's and Habener's early peptide work should be weighed; I cannot resolve priority from the evidence supplied.
For B006, whether Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer is the same achievement as CAR design, and how to handle Eshhar's absence from the credited names.
How much the still accumulating long-term safety data for the incretin class should shape the wording of the citation.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no documented personal or institutional connection to any credited candidate on any shortlisted ballot. My field, autoimmunity, is near cGAS-STING and CAR-T in autoimmune applications, but I do not infer a connection from shared topics or from my KI and Bergen affiliations.
